headline: A 1996 executive order links federal government contracting to employers' compliance with certain U.S. immigration law provisions.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order ties the federal government's buying of goods and services to whether contractors follow certain parts of the Immigration and Nationality Act. The title presents this as a way to make government purchasing more economical and efficient. No summary was provided, so the specific rules, penalties, and enforcement steps are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses that hold or seek federal government contracts
who_it_affects.how: Their compliance with certain immigration law provisions, likely including rules on hiring workers, may affect whether they can do business with the federal government.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that buy goods and services
who_it_affects.how: They would be expected to consider contractors' compliance with these immigration law provisions when awarding or managing contracts.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed February 13, 1996; no separate start date is given in the available information.
